summary:
Dominik Tornow outlines Resonate's working theory that general-purpose software implementations will be replaced by bespoke implementations generated on demand by coding agents, shifting reuse upstream from implementations to specifications. In this model, the specification becomes the product and the prompt becomes the platform. Resonate, a durable execution platform with SDKs in TypeScript, Python, Rust, Go, and Java, is repositioning so its value lives in its specification and protocol rather than its reference implementation, enabling infrastructure partners to derive durable execution natively on their stacks with minimal dependencies.

The core challenge is repeatedly synthesizing trusted, target-specific implementations from one abstract specification that makes no assumptions about concrete databases, schemas, or consistency models. Early attempts to have agents jump directly from abstract spec to concrete implementation (e.g., Rust on Postgres) failed—systems worked on happy paths but broke under concurrency, process failure, and network failure. Inserting a human-driven concrete specification as an intermediary artifact solved implementation but revealed that agents could build systems yet not design them.

The breakthrough came by giving agents a deterministic simulation environment in Python and asking them to first build a simulated implementation as executable design, then derive a concrete specification, and only then write the production implementation. This moved agents upstream into the design process. Two enablers are minimalism and simplicity: Resonate spent three years reducing its protocol to two core objects (durable promise and durable task).

Using NATS.io as the target platform—whose primitives include queues, a versioned key-value store, and delayed messages—the talk details the challenge of stale reads under NATS's consistency model and how the deterministic simulation environment exposes such behavior, including forbidden fruit information that production code cannot depend on but agents can use for debugging. This approach let the agent close the gap: building a fuzz-tested proof of concept in simulation, deriving a concrete specification from it, and then implementing production code. Tornow concludes that deterministic simulation lets agents participate in design, not just implementation, with humans still involved but the agent now as driver. From a single abstract specification, the agent designed and built the platform through simulation → concrete specification → concrete implementation.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

sections.title: Introduction: The Prompt is the Platform
sections.summary: Tornow introduces the thesis that coding agents will retire general-purpose platforms in favor of bespoke implementations generated on demand, shifting reuse upstream from implementations to specifications. Resonate is introduced as a durable execution platform, and the talk frames the core question: if implementations become generatable, value must move to the specification.

sections.title: Resonate's Repositioning and the Specification Challenge
sections.summary: Resonate repositions its product from implementation to specification/protocol, aiming to derive multiple server implementations including a reference implementation and partner-specific builds. The core challenge is repeatedly synthesizing trusted servers from the same abstract specification, which must not assume any concrete implementation details.

sections.title: First Attempt: Abstract Spec to Concrete Implementation (Failed)
sections.summary: Asking the agent to build a Resonate server in Rust on Postgres directly from the abstract spec failed. The system passed basic happy-path tests but broke under concurrency, process failure, and network failure—closer to a prototype than production. The gap between abstract spec and concrete implementation was too large.

sections.title: Intermediary Concrete Specification and Its Limitations
sections.summary: Inserting a human-driven concrete specification (data schema, indices, SQL queries, transaction boundaries) as an intermediary artifact enabled correct implementation. However, this revealed that the agent could build but not design the system, which is insufficient when the specification is a reusable product.

sections.title: Moving Agents Upstream via Deterministic Simulation
sections.summary: For Resonate on NATS.io, the approach changed: agents were given a deterministic simulation environment and asked to build a simulated implementation first as executable design, then derive a concrete specification, and only then write production code. The pipeline became abstract specification → simulation → concrete specification → concrete implementation, with agents now driving design.

sections.title: Minimalism, Simplicity, and the NATS Target Platform
sections.summary: Minimalism and simplicity are the finish line, not the starting point. Three years of reduction yielded a protocol with two objects: durable promise and durable task. NATS provides queues, a versioned key-value store, and delayed messages. The design question is expressing the Resonate protocol using only these primitives, complicated by stale reads in NATS's consistency model.

sections.title: Deterministic Simulation Environment and Forbidden Fruit
sections.summary: A deterministic simulation environment in Python simulates NATS IO components, including a key-value store with full version history, controlled stale reads, and optimistic concurrency enforcement. The simulation exposes forbidden fruit—information hidden in production such as whether a read was fresh or stale and the hidden latest value—which agents can use for debugging but production code cannot depend on. This causal feedback let the agent close the gap: proof of concept in simulation (fuzz-tested) → concrete specification → production implementation.

sections.title: Conclusion: Agent as Design Driver
sections.summary: Tornow concludes that deterministic simulation lets agents participate in design, not just implementation, with humans still involved but the agent now as driver. From a single abstract specification, the agent designed and built the platform through simulation → concrete specification → concrete implementation. The prompt is the platform; the specification is the product. He invites questions via Resonate's Discord.
